mainEntity.name: Are there hidden costs in social media marketing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common “hidden” cost is ad spend that isn't clearly separated from the management fee — always confirm which is which. Other add-ons to ask about include influencer fees, professional video production, premium design, extra platforms, and paid tools. A transparent provider lists these upfront rather than surprising you later.

mainEntity.name: Is VAT charged on social media marketing services in Saudi Arabia?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Saudi Arabia applies a standard VAT rate of 15%, and VAT-registered agencies must add it to their fees. So a SAR 10,000/month quote is effectively SAR 11,500 with VAT. Always check whether a quoted price includes VAT or not.

mainEntity.name: How long is a typical contract?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contracts commonly run for three, six, or twelve months. Three months is a reasonable trial period to judge results. Be cautious about long lock-ins with no early review clause — good providers are comfortable proving their value over a shorter initial term.

mainEntity.name: When should I increase my social media budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: Increase spend when the numbers justify it — when your ads are profitably generating leads or sales and you're confident more budget means more results. Scaling a campaign that's already working is one of the best investments you can make; scaling one that isn't just loses money faster.

mainEntity.name: What ROI should I expect from social media marketing?

acceptedAnswer.text: It varies by industry, offer, and budget, so be wary of anyone quoting a fixed multiple. Realistically, expect the first 1–3 months to build foundations, with measurable returns growing from there. The right metric isn't likes — it's leads, sales, and cost-per-result relative to what a customer is worth to you.

mainEntity.name: Do I need content in both Arabic and English?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Saudi businesses, yes. Arabic connects you authentically with local audiences, while English can be important for expatriate customers and certain B2B or international segments. Quality bilingual content sometimes costs slightly more, but it significantly widens your reach and credibility.

mainEntity.name: How much should a small business spend to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: A practical starting point is around SAR 2,000–4,000/month for management plus SAR 1,500–3,000/month for ad spend, focused on one or two platforms. That combined budget is usually the minimum required to move beyond simply “being present” toward generating real engagement and leads.

mainEntity.name: Which platform is best for my business in Saudi Arabia?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your audience. Consumer and retail brands often do best on Snapchat, TikTok, and Instagram, given how dominant they are locally. B2B and professional services usually get more value from LinkedIn. Most businesses benefit from two well-chosen platforms rather than spreading thin across all of them.

mainEntity.name: Can I do social media marketing myself instead of paying someone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can handle basics like replying to messages and simple posts yourself. Where outside help pays off is strategy, consistent quality content, video editing, and paid ad management — the areas where time and expertise directly affect results, and where costly mistakes are easy to make.

mainEntity.name: Why do prices vary so much between providers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because “social media marketing” covers very different scopes. Differences in the number of platforms, content volume, video production, community management, strategy, and whether you hire a freelancer or a full team can easily create a 10x price gap. Compare deliverables side by side, not just headline prices.
